bull.b: A predominantly recurring revenue base can improve visibility and reduce reliance on repeatedly winning new contracts. Long-term operator relationships also create opportunities to expand content, platforms, and services within existing deployments, supporting more durable revenue and cash generation.

The substantial EBITDA margin improvement indicates stronger operating economics despite tax increases. If management sustains these gains through content performance and operating discipline, higher margins can support reinvestment, debt reduction, and improved resilience across business cycles.

A rising share of non-U.K. revenue reduces the company’s dependence on one national market and broadens its addressable operator base. Greater exposure to North America and Greece can support longer-term growth while diversifying the effects of country-specific regulation and taxes.

bear.b: High debt combined with a persistent equity deficit materially limits financial flexibility. The capital structure can absorb a meaningful portion of operating cash flow through financing needs, while leaving less capacity to withstand setbacks or fund growth without relying on refinancing or asset-level cash generation.

Recent top-line contraction and renewed net losses show that strong gross and EBITDA margins have not yet translated into stable bottom-line performance. Earnings volatility makes internal funding less dependable and increases the importance of sustained revenue recovery and consistent cash conversion.

The Brazil shutdown is delaying growth expectations and reducing guidance, while higher U.K. gaming taxes directly pressure future economics. Together, these regulatory headwinds can suppress revenue, EBITDA, and free-cash-flow conversion over the next several quarters even if operations improve elsewhere.
